transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-01-31
Start time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 54 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Patel (Redwood AE), Sofia Ruiz (Redwood SE), Amir Li (Redwood CSM); Carlos Mendes (BlueArc Procurement), Lina Park (BlueArc Legal), Hannah Cole (BlueArc FinOps), Devon Reyes (BlueArc Cloud Ops)
Shared links: playbook draft (Redwood link), sample billing matrix (BlueArc link)

Summary:
Quick kickoff to align the FinOps approval path with the MSA/DPA redlines and how billing classification will flow for the pilot. Primary goals: define legal playbook handoff, confirm finance chargeback mapping, agree on technical deep dives (SSO/KMS) and timing for exec signoff.

Topics covered:
- FinOps approval matrix and chargeback codes
- Legal playbook and redline expectations (MSA/DPA special clauses around data residency and audit logs)
- SLA/billing interplay for pilot vs production
- Technical handoffs: SSO, KMS/HSM, VPC peering
- Timeline and decision gates

Action items (verbal recap at end): Jordan to send playbook template, Hannah to send FinOps matrix, Sofia to schedule SSO/KMS deep dive, Carlos to confirm billing owner and codes.

Transcript:
[00:00] Jordan Patel: All right thanks everyone for joining, really appreciate squeezing this in. Um, this is the kickoff to map FinOps approval path to our legal playbook, so we can get the pilot billing mapped correctly and get, you know, the MSA/DPA alignment moving.
[00:16] Carlos Mendes: Yep thanks Jordan, and thank you Sofia and Amir. On our side we have Hannah for FinOps, Lina for legal, and Devon for cloud ops. We, um, we want to make sure the cost center mapping is clear before procurement greenlights the pilot.
[00:29] Hannah Cole: Yeah hi all, small ask from me: I need to know how chargeback codes map to usage buckets — embeddings vs generation vs batch scoring — cause our cost allocation needs to be done at the pilot stage.
[00:43] Sofia Ruiz: Makes sense. We have a recommended billing matrix in the sample docs, but typically teams map model families and endpoint types to chargeback categories. We can adapt it to your internal codes, that's straightforward.
[00:57] Lina Park: Quick legal note, when you say MSA redlines, can you call out the typical DPA exceptions? We have strict data residency clauses for European customers and also audit rights that we need to log.
[01:12] Jordan Patel: For sure. Our playbook template calls out standard MSA language and a DPA appendix. We sometimes get asked for an addendum for on-prem/private deployments. There was a note though — sorry, sometimes our export says Redwood Dedicated as Dedicared — there's little transcription typos in the sample but the substance is Dedicated.
[01:33] Devon Reyes: From an ops perspective we need to confirm KMS or HSM integration — we can't have keys leaving our VPC for pilot. Is that supported?
[01:44] Sofia Ruiz: Yes, we support both customer-managed KMS and HSM integrations for Private deployments; for Hosted we offer envelope encryption with Redwood KMS but can also bring-your-own-KMS for VPC-connected flows. We'll cover specifics in the technical deep dive.
[01:59] Hannah Cole: And SLA-wise, if we start with Hosted for faster time to value, how do we model the SLA differences against charges if we later move to Dedicated? Any billing proration we should see?
[02:13] Amir Li: Good question. Typically the commercial team builds the pilot as a usage baseline and we do a short-term credit/commit arrangement. If you convert to Dedicated there's usually a migration credit and pricing re-baselining. Billing proration for partial months does happen, we can get finance to outline exact rules.
[02:31] Carlos Mendes: We need that spelled out in the playbook. Procurement needs a clear path: pilot acceptance criteria, billing posture, and legal readiness.
[02:43] Jordan Patel: Absolutely. Lina, would it help if we share a sample redline and a playbook with explicit decision gates?
[02:50] Lina Park: Yes that would be great. Also flag any clauses about your subprocessing list and the audit log retention — that's a hot button for us.
[03:01] Jordan Patel: Noted. We'll include the subprocessors as an appendix and call out audit log retention windows. We usually offer 90 days by default and extended retention as an add-on; we can surface that.
[03:12] Hannah Cole: For FinOps approval, the matrix is two-tiered: first approval from manager + FinOps, then exec signoff for anything over X dollars per month. I'll share the matrix after this call.
[03:25] Jordan Patel: Perfect. For the billing classification, can you walk us through the codes you use, Hannah?
[03:30] Hannah Cole: Sure, uh we use cost-centers like CC-PLAT-001 for platform infra, CC-ML-002 for model spend, and CC-RND-003 for R&D. For pilot we want model spend routed to CC-ML-002 but broken down per endpoint so we can see embeddings vs gen.
[03:46] Sofia Ruiz: We can emit usage reports at the token-level and label them by endpoint and model. If you want per-endpoint tracking we recommend route-level tokens so the billing CSV has columns for endpoint_name, model_id, tokens_in, tokens_out.
[04:02] Devon Reyes: On connectivity, we will require VPC peering for the pilot and customer-managed KMS. Also need to confirm that KV cache doesn't cache PII permanently — any TTL controls?
[04:15] Sofia Ruiz: TTLs are configurable at the cache layer; the store is in-memory for ephemeral cache by default, but we can configure eviction policies and brief retention windows. We'll capture those options in the technical appendix.
[04:29] Lina Park: A couple of items from security — we need SOC 2 attestations and an updated encryption footprint doc. Can you add those to the playbook?
[04:38] Jordan Patel: Yes we'll attach the SOC2 summary and the encryption architecture. Also will include our pen test cadence and contact for security questionnaires.
[04:46] Carlos Mendes: On procurement timeline, our aim is to have pilot approvals by Feb 20 and start integration Feb 23. Is that feasible?
[04:55] Jordan Patel: That seems doable if we get the FinOps matrix and legal redlines within the next two weeks. So action wise: we'll send the playbook by Feb 2, you send the approval matrix by Feb 6, technical deep dive the week of Feb 9, and then target procurement approval Feb 20.
[05:12] Hannah Cole: That schedule works for us if we can see the billing matrix before our next finance sync.
[05:19] Amir Li: Noted — we'll watch for that. Also, Carlos, is there a preferred format for the redlines? Word track changes or a PDF annotated?
[05:29] Lina Park: Word redlines please, we need to push them through our legal tooling.
[05:33] Sofia Ruiz: Good, we'll send a Word playbook and a one-page summary for procurement.
[05:40] Jordan Patel: Quick thought — regarding pricing approvals, do you have a procurement threshold we should be aware of that would require exec involvement?
[05:48] Carlos Mendes: Yes anything above 75k ARR needs VP approval, and above 200k goes to procurement committee. Pilot is expected to be well under that but if it scales we'll need to re-engage.
[06:00] Hannah Cole: Also note we have an internal requirement to tag spend by product line in our cost allocation tooling. So the output columns from Redwood's billing CSV need to be stable.
[06:11] Sofia Ruiz: We'll confirm the CSV schema and lock the fields for the pilot. If changes are needed later we can version the schema but we'll keep it stable for the pilot.
[06:21] Devon Reyes: What's the structure for the pilot SLO? We need to know latency targets for production vs pilot so we can align monitoring and alerting.
[06:31] Amir Li: Typically for pilot we set a softer latency SLO, e.g., p95 under 600ms for generation for small models, and then tighten at production. We can include default SLO templates in the playbook.
[06:44] Jordan Patel: Great. I'm also going to flag that if you need on-prem or private deployment the legal and FinOps flows change slightly because of licensing and hosting fees. We'll call that out.
[06:55] Lina Park: One more detail on audit logs: we need an export format consumable by our SIEM, ideally syslog or S3 CSV with timestamps.
[07:04] Sofia Ruiz: We can provide S3 exports and a syslog stream. We'll document the formats and sample payloads.
[07:13] Carlos Mendes: Sounds good. Any competitors or alternate vendors to mention? We also assessed AuroraAI last quarter.
[07:20] Jordan Patel: We know AuroraAI is often compared; our differentiation is the routing and cost controls plus the unified private/hosted flow. But we won't get into a feature war here, we want to get the playbook in your hands.
[07:31] Hannah Cole: Ok quick logistics — can you include a short section in the playbook that outlines post-pilot conversion economics? That helps our finance modelers.
[07:42] Jordan Patel: Yes we'll add a conversion appendix with example math.
[07:46] Amir Li: Recap of next steps: Jordan sends playbook and redlines by Feb 2; Hannah sends FinOps matrix and SOW by Feb 6; Sofia schedules technical deep dive week of Feb 9; Carlos confirms billing owner and chargeback codes by Feb 13.
[07:58] Carlos Mendes: Confirmed. Also I'll put a tentative Exec review on Feb 19 in case we need it.
[08:04] Lina Park: We'll get Word redlines back quickly once we see the template.
[08:08] Jordan Patel: Great. Thanks everyone — look forward to the deep dive.
[08:12] Meeting end

Notes on transcript quality: Some automatic timestamps and product names may be slightly off; e.g., Dedicared vs Dedicated, Redwood Optimize spelled differently by speech-to-text. Natural hesitations and crosstalk present.

End of transcript.
